## Import Parser Generation — Complete

**Project type:** `da` (Document Authoring) — no xwalk requirements applied.

**Variants processed:** 4 of 4 (all had cached block context; none skipped).

| Variant | Base block | Parser file | Instances validated | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cards-feature | cards (2-col) | `tools/importer/parsers/cards-feature.js` | 14 (3× `.teaser.basemarketingproperties` + 11× `.iconcard`) | Passed |
| carousel-promo | carousel (2-col, 1 row/slide) | `tools/importer/parsers/carousel-promo.js` | `.slider-container` (promocards) + `.course-card-slider.contentfragmentlist` (course cards) | Passed |
| cards-overlay | cards (2-col) | `tools/importer/parsers/cards-overlay.js` | 6× `.imagetile` | Passed |
| hero-home | hero (1-col, image + content rows) | `tools/importer/parsers/hero-home.js` | `.hero.cmp-hero__banner-center--large` | Passed |

**Validation:** Every parser passed the PostToolUse hook on the first attempt, with `captureConfident: true` on all instances and `blockText` matching `sourceText`. No iterations were required.

**Key design decisions:**
- All parsers use the mandatory contract: `export default function parse(element, { document })`, `WebImporter.Blocks.createBlock(document, { name, cells })` with the exact variant name, and `element.replaceWith(block)` (no return).
- **cards-feature / cards-overlay:** Each matched element is a single card → one 2-column row `[image, contentCell]`, with `''` padding when no image is present to keep column count consistent.
- **carousel-promo:** Iterates `.swiper-slide` (promocards instance) with a fallback to `.promocards`/`.course-card`/`.cmp-teaser` for the `.course-card-slider.contentfragmentlist` instance; emits one 2-column row per slide. Promo card labels are wrapped in a `<p>` so they survive as text content, and both button1/button2 CTAs are captured.
- **hero-home:** 1-column layout — optional background-image row, then a single content cell holding heading + subheading + any CTAs.
- All selectors were validated against each variant's `source.html`, with defensive fallbacks added for cross-page/cross-instance DOM variation.

### What happened
The boilerplate CSS shipped with this block was a full-bleed **hero** carousel (single 100%-width slide, absolute-positioned background image, dark text overlay box). The source `.slider-container` is instead a **multi-card horizontal card carousel**, so I replaced the CSS entirely with values extracted from the source's computed styles.

Key extracted/applied values:
- Card: `border-radius: 24px`, `1px solid rgb(225 229 234)`, shadow `rgb(0 0 0 /10%) 0 4px 6px -1px, rgb(0 0 0 /6%) 0 2px 4px -1px`, `padding: 24px`, white background.
- Image: `border-radius: 12px`, `object-fit: cover`.
- Eyebrow label: `16px/600`, `uppercase`, `letter-spacing 0.8px`, color `rgb(96 118 144)`.
- Title `h6`: `23px/600`, `line-height 1.2`, `letter-spacing -0.575px`, dark text; highlighted words (`.cmp-text--blue`) mapped to `--link-hover-color`.
- Buttons: pill `border-radius: 50px`; primary filled uses `--link-hover-color` (rgb 15 98 254) white text; tertiary link uses `rgb(51 63 76)` with an arrow glyph.
- Responsive: 1 card mobile → 2 at ≥600px → 3 at ≥900px, matching the source's per-breakpoint show counts. Dot indicators hidden (source disables pagination — arrows only).

### Notable EDS handling
- The two source instances (promo product cards, course cards) share the same block. They differ by content order — promo = eyebrow→title→CTAs, course = image→title→uppercase label. I distinguish them purely with `:has(> h6:first-child)` to switch text alignment (centered vs left) with no JS change.
- Instance 1 sits inside a `blue` section. The global `main .section.blue h6 {color: light}` rule was overriding the card title, rendering it near-white. Fixed by prefixing the title rule with `main .section` to win specificity and keep card titles dark.

The critical discovery was that on this site **each feature card is authored as its own `cards-feature` block** (a single `<li>`). ## Summary

**File changed:** `/workspace/current/blocks/cards-quote/cards-quote.css` (rewritten; `cards-quote.js` untouched)

### Bug 1 — Layout (3-across, full width)
Because each card is authored as its own `cards-quote` block, EDS renders them as sibling `.cards-quote-wrapper` divs inside `.section.cards-quote-container`. The old CSS only styled `.cards-quote > ul` internally (each block was a lone narrow column), so I applied the multi-card grid at the **section-container level** — matching the established `cards-feature` / `cards-overlay` pattern:
- `main .section.cards-quote-container` → `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 24px; max-width: 1248px; margin: 40px auto`
- Responsive card cells: 1-across mobile → 2-across at `≥600px` → 3-across at `≥900px` (`flex: 1 1 calc(33.333% - 16px)`), heading spans full width
- `align-items: stretch` + `height: 100%` on the `li` gives equal-height cards

Verified: the 3 wrappers now share `top: 1897`, at `left: 96 / 520 / 944`, each `width: 400px`.

### Bug 2 — Dark-section styling (from source computed styles)
- Card surface (`> ul > li`): `background: rgb(41 51 61)`, `border: 1px solid rgb(62 77 92)`, `border-radius: 24px`, source box-shadow, `padding: 24px` — replacing the old white bg + grey border
- Heading `h5`: `var(--section-light-text)` (rgb 250 250 250), 28px/600, line-height 33.6px, letter-spacing -0.7px — now readable (was white-on-white)
- Body `p`: `rgb(217 228 240)`, 16px/400/24px, letter-spacing -0.4px
- CTA link (last `<p><a>`): accent `rgb(207 234 0)`, weight 600, `inline-flex` with a trailing `→` arrow via `::after`, pushed to the card bottom with `margin-top: auto` for equal-height alignment. Also covered the `a.button` variant in case EDS buttonizes the link.

### Validation
- Visual screenshot of §8 preview matches source: 3 dark cards side-by-side, full content width, readable light headings/body, accent CTAs.
- CTA computed style confirmed: `color rgb(207,234,0)`, `font-weight 600`, arrow `"→"`.
- `npx stylelint blocks/cards-quote/cards-quote.css` → exit 0, no issues.

Visual match: ~95% (Excellent). No remaining gaps. `cards-quote.js` was not modified.

3. **No accordion / no drill-in.** Tapping a top item does nothing useful; there's no chevron affordance and no way to focus one section.

### Original site pattern (the target)

- **Closed toolbar:** logo · search icon · hamburger.
- **Level 1 (hamburger open):** a full-screen opaque overlay showing only the 5 top items, large and stacked, with a **close (×)** top-right and **Log In / Register** pinned at the bottom. Each item has a **chevron (›)**.
- **Level 2 (tap an item → drill-in / slide):** replaces the list with that section's panel — a **back arrow (←)** + **close (×)**, the section title as a link ("Explore at DS →"), then the category headings (Digital Dentistry, Restorative, …) each with an expand **chevron (˅)**, followed by the quick links and featured box.
- **Level 3 (tap a category → accordion in place):** the chevron flips (˄) and that category expands to show "Explore all … →", **BRANDS** list, **PRODUCT TOPICS** list, while sibling categories stay collapsed.

**Scope:** phone + tablet (`< 900px`); desktop mega-menu is untouched. Changes limited to `blocks/header/header.js` and `blocks/header/header.css` (behavioral/CSS only — no content or import changes).

### A. Fix the overlay shell (both breakpoints)
1. When open, make `header nav` a **fixed, full-viewport, opaque overlay** (`--page-bg` background, `position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index` above page, `overflow-y: auto`) so nothing behind shows through. Keep `body { overflow: hidden }` (already present) to lock background scroll.
2. Toolbar row inside the overlay: brand on the left, **× close** on the right (repurpose the hamburger button — it already toggles `aria-label` Open/Close; style its icon as an X when `nav[aria-expanded="true"]`).

### B. Level 1 → 2: drill-in instead of expand-all

6. Tapping a top item on mobile sets only *that* item to expanded and adds a `nav--drilled` state; CSS **hides the level-1 list and slides in the section panel** (translateX transition for the push effect). Show a **back arrow** that clears the drilled state and returns to level 1.

### C. Level 3: category accordion within a drilled section

### Assistant [2026-09-09 01:00:59 UTC]

The full page renders cleanly with consistent, harmonious rhythm throughout — every section now has the same title→cards and cards→CTA spacing, and uniform top/bottom padding. No visual regressions, no console errors.

The section spacing is now governed by a single overarching design system. Here's what I did:

## The problem
Each card block was independently redefining the title→cards gap with different hardcoded values:
- cards-feature: 40px (but rendering 64px due to double-counting)
- cards-overlay: 36px
- cards-quote: 24px

And the cards→CTA gap was only defined in one block. The result: inconsistent rhythm from section to section.

## The design-system solution
I centralized the vertical rhythm in `styles.css` with two global rules that apply to **every** section, keyed on the consistent authoring structure (leading `.default-content-wrapper` = title, trailing one = CTA):

```css
main > .section > .default-content-wrapper:first-child        { margin: 0 0 var(--section-heading-gap); }
main > .section > .default-content-wrapper:last-child:not(:first-child) { margin: var(--section-heading-gap) 0 0; }
```

Both gaps derive from the existing `--section-heading-gap` token (40px) — the single source of truth, alongside the already-global `--section-padding-block` (64px) for top/bottom padding.

## Cleanup
- **Removed** the hardcoded `36px` and `24px` overrides from cards-overlay and cards-quote.
- Blocks that use a flex/grid **row-gap** (cards-feature, cards-overlay, cards-quote) would otherwise double-count the gap on top of the global margin, so each subtracts exactly one `--grid-gap` increment (`calc(var(--section-heading-gap) - var(--grid-gap))`) — a small, self-documenting adjustment so the *effective* gap lands at the same 40px everywhere. The `carousel-promo` section (no row-gap) uses the global value directly.

## Result — verified
Every section now measures an identical **40px title→cards gap** and **40px cards→CTA gap**, plus the already-uniform **64px top/bottom padding** (hero excepted, intentionally flush to the nav). A section that genuinely needs different spacing can still override locally, but none need to redefine the default anymore. All CSS lints clean and there are no visual regressions or console errors.

## What the user reported
In the §3 "Digitize" teaser cards: too little bottom padding, and too much space between title (e.g. "Diagnose") and description.

## Root causes found
1. **Bottom padding** was overridden to 12px on teaser cards (too cramped).
2. **Title→description gap was 24px** despite an 8px title margin — because the description paragraph, being the card's last child when there's no CTA, was wrongly inheriting the 16px CTA-gap rule (`p:last-child`).

## Design-system tokenization
Following your approach — define the average that fits most cards, let outliers override — I added three card-rhythm tokens to `brand.css`:
- `--card-title-gap: 8px` — title → description
- `--card-cta-gap: 16px` — description → CTA
- (kept existing `--card-padding: 24px`, `--radius-card`, `--shadow-card`, etc.)

Then I made the shared `.cards-feature` typography use these as the **default**, and removed the redundant per-variant overrides that were just re-stating the same values:
- Deleted two duplicate title-gap overrides (teaser + icon-card both re-declared 8px → now inherited).

- Removed the redundant 12px/16px bottom-padding overrides → both variants now use the uniform 24px `--card-padding`.
- **Scoped the CTA gap to real CTAs** (`p:last-child:has(a)`) so a plain description never inherits it.
- Removed the double CTA margins (kept the gap only on the wrapping paragraph).

## Result (verified across card types)
- Title → description: **uniform 8px** everywhere (was 24px on teasers)
- Description → CTA: **uniform 16px** (was 32px double-counted)
- Card bottom padding: **uniform 24px** (was 12px)

### How the import script now detects section styles

The top-level pages don't use a fixed section list — they're flattened into sections at heading boundaries — so section styling wasn't being applied at all. I added **automatic background detection** to the importer:

1. During page load (where computed styles are available), for each section heading it walks up to the nearest full-width band and reads its actual background color.
2. It maps the color to a brand style name — dark slate → `dark`, light grey → `grey`, white → default (no style) — and stamps the heading.
3. In the flattening step, each styled section now emits a **Section Metadata** block with the detected style, so the section renders with the correct background.

This is generic: it will correctly pick up dark/grey section bands on any of the top-level pages, not just Support, and it correctly left the FAQ accordion and other white sections on the default background (no false positives).

The corrected Support page is **published live** on the EDS preview at `/en-us/support`, verified with the right backgrounds.

## Summary

**Root cause:** The importer captured some images as **raw DAM download URLs** (`/content/dam/…jpg|png`) that serve the full-resolution originals (23–39 MB) and — unlike Scene7 URLs — ignore resize parameters. EDS refuses to preview/publish any page referencing an image over 20 MB, so these four pages failed to deploy.

**Fixed images** (7 oversized originals, shared across the 4 pages):

| Image | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| dsc-digital-dentistry-hub-ds-core-next-level | 39.0 MB | 0.4 MB |
| SUSM Primescan Course Banner | 33.4 MB | 0.3 MB |
| CORP-image-professional-education-dentist | 27.1 MB | 0.2 MB |
| CE-Clinical-Image-hands-on-Aligner-02 | 27.0 MB | 0.3 MB |
| PPS-workflow-image-lab-owner-inLab-SW | 25.0 MB | 0.3 MB |
| CE-Clinical-Image-digital-learning-02 | 24.0 MB | 0.3 MB |
| dsc-digital-dentistry-hub-possibilities | 23.3 MB | 0.2 MB |

Each was downloaded, resized to max 2000px wide (ample for full-width display), stripped of metadata, and re-encoded at JPEG quality 82 — a >98% size cut with **no visible quality loss** (verified in the render).

**How I fixed it:**
1. Optimized the 7 images with ImageMagick, saved to `content/images/`.
2. Rewrote the 4 pages' references to `/en-us/images/<name>.jpg` (the EDS-served path; the local dev server proxies it, so it renders in both environments).
3. Uploaded all 7 images to Document Authoring and triggered their previews.
4. Re-uploaded + previewed all 4 pages.

**Importer improvement for the future:** Added `tools/importer/optimize-oversized-images.js` — a reusable, idempotent post-import step that scans all imported pages, detects any DAM image over the threshold, downloads + optimizes it, and rewrites references automatically. Scene7 URLs are left untouched (already served resized). Lint-clean.

**Verification:**
- All 4 pages: **preview 200, page 200** — deploy successfully, no more oversized-image failures.
- All 7 optimized images serve on EDS (200, image/jpeg) and render correctly.
- Confirmed none of the optimized images are broken; the optimizer is idempotent (re-run reports "nothing to do").

Note: the images and page content publish via Document Authoring (done); the new optimizer **script** is a code file that would reach `main` on the next authorized git push (the same pending push from the nav/footer fix), but it isn't needed for these four pages — they're already fixed and live.

## Summary

I added a **persistent active-section underline** to the top navigation, implemented generically from the page hierarchy.

**How it works:**
- In `header.js`, after the nav is decorated, it reads the current page's path (stripping the local `/content` prefix and `.html`/trailing slash so it matches in both the dev server and EDS), then for each top-level nav item derives that item's own section path from its `href` and finds the one whose section is a **path-segment prefix** of the current page (longest/most-specific wins). That item gets a `.nav-active` class.
- In `header.css`, the underline (and blue text) rule now fires for `.nav-active` **in addition to** `:hover` and the open-panel `[aria-expanded='true']` state.

**Behavior:**
- The active section's underline stays visible on its top-level page and every descendant.
- Because active and hover are independent CSS conditions, hovering a different item shows **both** underlines at once.
- Fully generic — no per-page rules; adding new sections/pages needs no changes.

**Verified locally across all sections + nested pages:**

I think that this is the associated rule that you should follow for all styles and that you broke in this specific case:
R2. **Layout classes go on generated wrapper elements, never on the authored
    element.** The editor swap (`replaceWith`) destroys anything set on the
    authored element, mid-session. Pattern:
    ```js
    // WRONG — class and identity die in the editor swap / rebuild
    const t = document.createElement('p');
    t.className = 'card-title';
    t.textContent = cell.textContent.trim();
    // RIGHT — wrapper carries layout; authored element moves in whole
    const t = document.createElement('div');
    t.className = 'card-title';
    t.append(...[...cell.children].filter((n) => n.textContent.trim()));
    ```

Fix this for us to test whether that fixes the style issue when editing this page.

## Audit report: WYSIWYG editor-safety across homepage blocks

**Scope audited:** every block used on the homepage — `hero-home`, `carousel-promo`, `cards-feature`, `cards-overlay`, `cards-quote` — plus the shared `header` and `footer`. Method: for each block, cross-referenced JS class/ID injection against the CSS selectors that depend on it, isolating any case where a **class lives on an authored/editable leaf element** (heading, paragraph, link, image, list item) that the editor rebuilds mid-session.

### Issue found & fixed

**1. `cards-overlay` — CTA class on the authored `<a>`**
- **File:** `blocks/cards-overlay/cards-overlay.js` + `blocks/cards-overlay/cards-overlay.css`
- **Unsafe pattern:** JS did `a.classList.add('cards-overlay-cta')` directly on the authored link, and the CSS depended on `a.cards-overlay-cta` (`:any-link`, `::after` arrow, hover). When the WYSIWYG editor rebuilds the `<a>`/`<p>` during editing, that runtime class is dropped and the CTA reverts to a plain link mid-session (identical to the `carousel-promo` bug).
- **Fix:** JS now moves the authored `<p><a>` **intact** into a generated `<div class="cards-overlay-cta">`; the `<a>` gets **no** injected class (EDS button classes are still stripped). CSS now targets the stable wrapper: `.cards-overlay-cta a` (+ `.cards-overlay-cta > p` margin reset). DOM stays minimal — one wrapper per CTA.
- **Verified:** normal preview renders identically (inline-flex, white text, arrow glyph, hugged content); and simulating the editor replacing the `<a>` with a fresh class-less element, the CTA **stayed fully styled** because the selector keys off the wrapper.

*(`carousel-promo` was the same class of bug, fixed in the prior turn — re-verified clean here.)*

### Cases intentionally left unchanged (and why)

- **`cards-feature` / `cards-quote`** — classes (`cards-feature-card-image/-body`, `cards-quote-card-image/-body`, `cards-feature-card-icon`) go only on **generated cell/wrapper `<div>`s** the block owns. All authored elements (`h5/h6/p/a`) are styled as **bare-tag descendants** of those wrappers, never via a class on themselves. Editor-safe as-is.
- **`hero-home`** — only adds `.no-image`/`.shop` to the **block root**, not to authored content.
- **`.button`/`.primary`/`.secondary`/`.accent`** (hero-home, cards-quote, others) — applied by the shared `scripts/scripts.js` button decoration, **derived from authored `<strong>`/`<em>` markup** and re-applied on every decoration pass. This is the framework-standard EDS pattern; it self-heals because the class is a pure function of markup the editor preserves.
- **`footer` accent links** — `footer-link-accent` is derived from authored `<em>` and, critically, has a CSS **fallback on `footer em`** so the orange renders even if the class is lost. Self-healing by design.
- **`header`** — decorates a hand-authored **fragment** (`nav.plain.html`), not page content edited via the page's WYSIWYG editor; its classes sit on structural `<li>`/section elements it rebuilds itself, and `nav-active` is URL-derived and re-applied each decorate.

### Reusable rule going forward

**Layout / structural / component-role classes belong on block-generated wrapper elements — never on authored, editable elements (headings, paragraphs, links, lists, images).** When a hook is needed around authored content, create a wrapper and move the authored element into it **intact** (never recreate its editable content), and write CSS as `.wrapper-class <tag>` rather than `<tag>.injected-class`. Only add a wrapper where a stable hook is genuinely required. Exceptions that remain safe are hooks *derived from authored markup and re-applied on every decoration* (like the `<strong>`→`.button` and `<em>`→accent conversions), especially when backed by a markup-based CSS fallback.

**It's neither a stale build nor exactly a cache issue on your end — the deployed footer genuinely was rendering grey, and I've now fixed the underlying cause.**

## What was wrong

The three `cards-promo` items on the Shop page share one flex row, and the card **wrappers** were already stretching to equal height (`align-items: stretch`). But the block element itself — `.cards-promo` (rendered `display: block`) — sat between the stretched wrapper and the `.cards-promo-card`. So on the shorter card (e.g. "ONE DS", a one-line title), the card only grew to its own content height inside the taller wrapper, leaving its bottom-pinned CTA (`margin-top: auto`) with no slack to push into. Result: at the 3-across widths, that card was shorter (339 vs 366px) and its CTA sat ~27px higher than the others.

At 1440px the titles happened to wrap to the same height so it looked fine — the break only showed at narrower widths where "Save up to $1,000…" and "Primescan 2 powered by DS Core" wrapped to two lines while "ONE DS" stayed one line.

## The fix

Added one reusable rule in `blocks/cards-promo/cards-promo.css` making the block a full-height flex column so the card fills its stretched wrapper:

```css
.cards-promo.block {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}
```

That lets `.cards-promo-card` (already `flex: 1 1 auto`) grow to the full wrapper height, giving the `margin-top: auto` CTA the space to drop to the card bottom — so all three CTAs land on one line.

## Verified across breakpoints

- **1440 / 1024 / 900 / 600px** (3-across row): all three cards equal height (366/366/437px) and all CTA tops identical → aligned on one horizontal line.
- **375px** (stacked single column): each card still pins its CTA to its own bottom with consistent padding; equal-height across a row doesn't apply since there's no row.

The change is scoped to the reusable `cards-promo` block styling and lints clean.

### User [2026-09-09 12:16:26 UTC]

Create some rules in # AGENTS.md about what you're not allowed to do to not break Experience Workspace authoring in AEM Edge Delivery:

# Generated blocks must preserve authored-element identity for Experience Workspace inline editing
## Problem
Blocks that rebuild authored content during decoration are invisible to
Experience Workspace (da.live) inline editing. On a representative generated
page, only 23 of 108 possible texts were editable; the rest were dead because
`decorate()` had discarded the elements the editor addresses.
This is not a styling bug or a missing feature flag. It follows from how the
workspace works, so it is a hard constraint on any system that emits
`decorate()` code.
## Why (the mechanism, verified against the da.live sources)
Experience Workspace never parses or maps the rendered DOM. It rents the
project's own render pipeline:
1. The preview host injects a bootstrap into `scripts.js` that hands the
   quick-edit plugin the page's own `loadPage()`.
2. The workspace serializes its collaborative ProseMirror document to HTML,
   stamping **document positions** as attributes: `data-prose-index` on every
   paragraph-level element, `data-image-index` on images, `data-block-index`
   on blocks. It swaps this into `document.body` and re-runs `loadPage()` —
   i.e. every block's `decorate()` runs over instrumented markup.
3. Every element still carrying `data-prose-index` **after decoration** is
   replaced in place by a live ProseMirror editor. Elements that lost the
   attribute are permanently uneditable — only `data-block-index` is repaired
   afterwards (by class-name matching), never `data-prose-index`.
4. Edits post the node back into the shared document; cursor math uses the
   element's exact `textContent` length, so displayed text must be the
   authored text verbatim.
Consequences: `textContent = x`, innerHTML rebuilds, `cloneNode` + discard,
and `.trim()` of displayed text all silently destroy editability. The
attribute is on the `<p>`/`<h*>`, not on inline children like `<a>`.
## Required generation rules
R1. **Move authored elements; never rebuild them.** Slot the authored
    `<p>`/`<h*>`/`<picture>` into the generated layout with `append()`. Do not
    re-create elements from `textContent`, do not clone-and-discard, do not
    retag (an authored `<h2>` stays an `<h2>`), do not trim or normalize
    displayed text.
R2. **Layout classes go on generated wrapper elements, never on the authored
    element.** The editor swap (`replaceWith`) destroys anything set on the
    authored element, mid-session. Pattern:
    ```js
    // WRONG — class and identity die in the editor swap / rebuild
    const t = document.createElement('p');
    t.className = 'card-title';
    t.textContent = cell.textContent.trim();
    // RIGHT — wrapper carries layout; authored element moves in whole
    const t = document.createElement('div');
    t.className = 'card-title';
    t.append(...[...cell.children].filter((n) => n.textContent.trim()));
    ```
R3. **Style through inheritance with explicit resets.** Typography lives on
    the wrapper; the inner authored element (or the editor that replaces it)
    gets `margin: 0; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-weight:
    inherit; color: inherit;`. The `color: inherit` is load-bearing: global
    element rules (e.g. `h1..h6 { color: ... }`) beat inherited values, in
    published and edit mode alike.
R4. **CTAs: move the paragraph, not the anchor.** The prose index sits on the
    `<p>`; `action.append(a.closest('p') || a)`. Button classes added to the
    anchor die during editing — provide the edit-mode look once, globally,
    derived from the authored `strong`/`em` convention and gated by
    `body.quick-edit` (set by the injected bootstrap; zero effect on
    published pages).
R5. **Card-as-link: unwrap the authored inner anchor in the live DOM**
    (`a.replaceWith(...a.childNodes)`) after capturing its href. The indexed
    paragraph survives; nested anchors are avoided; the link mark still lives
    in the source document. Editor-rendered anchors inside such cards need
    `color: inherit; text-decoration: none` where the global link ink clashes.
R6. **Text-as-metadata is exempt.** Authored text that is never displayed
    (glyph-lookup keys, label|value row labels, variant selectors) needs no
    inline editability — it is edited in the workspace's Content view. Derived
    UI text (tab labels mirroring panel titles) is edited through its source.
R7. **Adopted/nested content must also move.** A block that assembles sibling
    sections (tabs, accordions) must move the decorated blocks whole; their
    instrumentation carries over by identity. Re-running the assembly after a
    body swap must be idempotent (the workspace re-decorates on structural
    edits).
## Acceptance criteria (verifiable per generated block)
Given the page open in Experience Workspace with the block's branch
(`https://da.live/canvas?ref=<branch>#/<org>/<repo>/<path>`), after
instrumentation:
- [ ] every visible authored text in the block is inside a
      `div.prosemirror-editor` (count editors vs. authored text elements);
- [ ] typing in each editor updates the source document
      (`getInstrumentedHTML` contains the typed text) and the layout does not
      collapse while editing;
- [ ] computed color / font-size / font-weight of each text is identical in
      published mode and edit mode;
- [ ] the published page (no `quick-edit`) is byte-equivalent in rendering to
      the pre-change block: no nested anchors, hrefs intact, no color drift.
Note for automation: instrumentation only arrives on ProseMirror doc
transactions; trigger it deterministically by calling
`updateDocument(ewEditorDoc._controllerCtx)` from
`https://da.live/blocks/canvas/editor-utils/editor-utils.js` in the canvas
page context.
## Reference implementation
`keepthebyte/aem-marriott` PR #1 converts 8 block types (hero, join-band,
offer-band, benefits-card, explore-cards, carousel, tier-tabs, brand-strip)
to this contract, 23 → 108 editable texts, with the full contract and test
recipe in `docs/quick-edit.md`.
